stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: SpaceX’s ambitious, expensive gamble to replace AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon
stories.author: Nilay Patel
bullet_points: SpaceX is pursuing a major strategic shift to become a significant wireless carrier.
The plan involves acquiring substantial low-band spectrum to augment the Starlink network.
The move represents a high-stakes, capital-intensive entry into the established telecom market dominated by AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon.

stories.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Major AI players (OpenAI, Google, Meta) are heavily promoting autonomous AI agents capable of complex online tasks.
A significant emerging issue is the resistance from existing websites to allowing these AI agents to interact with them.
This signals a potential friction point or roadblock in the widespread adoption and functionality of autonomous AI agents.

stories.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: OpenAI models demonstrated the capability to hack a crypto wallet and breach multiple websites.
The incident highlights the advanced, potentially autonomous, capabilities of current AI models.
The actions performed by the AI were sophisticated enough to warrant criminal charges if executed by a human.

stories.title: Meta may use sweeping new commercial TOS to avoid millions in AI licensing fees
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta is reportedly updating its commercial Terms of Service (TOS).
The changes are seen by legal experts as a potential strategy to circumvent significant AI licensing costs.
The move is characterized as a major power consolidation play within the AI industry.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work advances the concept of AI for AI (AI4AI) and recursive self-improvement (RSI) by enabling AI systems to develop and improve themselves.
The system utilizes workflow-driven MLE and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon experimentation autonomously.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research proposes MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work advances the concept of AI for AI (AI4AI) and recursive self-improvement (RSI) by enabling LLMs to build and improve AI systems autonomously.
The system utilizes workflow-driven MLE orchestration and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon experimentation.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on practical LLM deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a generative AI model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in its MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Meta is revising its terms of service following public backlash regarding AI data scraping.
The change specifically removes language that implied Meta could use content from news sites to train its AI.
This signals increased regulatory and public scrutiny over how large tech companies utilize copyrighted web content for AI development.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
The benchmark moves beyond simple, well-defined tasks to model the ambiguity and complexity faced by Field Deployment Engineers (FDEs).
FDE-Gym comprises 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 real-world customer scenarios across 18 different industry sectors.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the field of AI for AI (AI4AI) and the concept of recursive self-improvement (RSI).
The model utilizes workflow-driven systems and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation.

stories.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
stories.author: Laurent Itti
bullet_points: Introduction of 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem designed to allow coding agents to generate editable and verifiable 3D content at scale.
The ecosystem includes a large-scale, high-quality dataset of executable 3D code, specifically 3DCodeVerse-2M.
It provides a coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification, advancing the field of 3D coding.

stories.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
stories.author: Tat-Seng Chua
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of 'goal drift' in complex LLM-based agents and multi-agent systems.
Proposes a novel 'steering agent' designed to supervise execution in real-time.
This steering mechanism actively corrects the system's trajectory when it deviates from the intended goal.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, Beam, available via Ollama.
Beam is specifically engineered for software engineering, reasoning, and complex agentic tasks.
The model is offered free for a limited time through Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure deployment of local AI models in the cloud.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
Decision models process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Mercedes-AMG’s first ground-up SUV is a 1,150hp electric beast
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Mercedes-AMG is introducing a new electric SUV, the 2028 AMG GT SUV.
The vehicle is positioned as a high-performance electric vehicle, comparable to the AMG GT coupe.
It features significant power, with the AMG brand known for high-output electric drivetrains.

stories.title: US Rep proposes bill to give video game buyers "ownership," not "a license"
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: A US Representative has introduced legislation aimed at granting video game buyers true 'ownership' of their purchases.
The proposal seeks to move beyond the current model where consumers only hold a 'license' to use the software.
The path to implementation faces substantial technical and legislative challenges.

stories.title: Bug turns one of the biggest fears about Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses into reality
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A significant privacy vulnerability was found in Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.
The reported bug, which realized a major user fear, has since been patched.
Despite the fix, underlying privacy concerns regarding the device remain a key issue.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for Personalized Robotic Manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in robotic agents.
Focuses on evaluating how policies adhere to user preferences, even in zero-shot learning scenarios.

stories.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
stories.author: Mikhail D. Lukin
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Large Language Models (LLMs) to discover advanced quantum circuits.
Developing efficient quantum algorithms is crucial for achieving practical quantum advantage.
The optimization process in quantum computing faces unique challenges, notably the reversibility constraint.

stories.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
stories.author: Yejin Choi
bullet_points: T2-z introduces a method for Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents in robotic world models.
The model addresses the challenge of predicting world responses by accounting for unobservable environmental factors (e.g., friction, mass).
It augments existing robotic world models with a compact, learnable latent variable to condition predictions on underlying environmental properties.

stories.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces CoDA, a framework for co-evolving simulation data engines and robot action policies.
Addresses the limitation of generative simulations by focusing on creating physically valid environments relevant to policy failures.
Utilizes a shared heterogeneous memory to track environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses routing exploration challenges in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It analyzes the interplay between fine-grained expert segmentation and the use of shared experts in MoE architectures.
A key dilemma identified is how shared experts can reduce the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in current 3D world models where geometry features from foundation models are view-dependent.
Introduces 'GeoState,' a novel view-decoupled geometry representation designed for predictive 3D world modeling.
The core innovation separates the scene's true state evolution from variations caused by the camera viewpoint.

stories.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
stories.author: Ruoshi Liu
bullet_points: Introduces DSP (Dexterity from supervised play), a framework for teaching robots complex manipulation.
The system uses behavior cloning on short human play sessions to generate an initial 'play policy'.
This policy is then used to guide autonomous data collection and train a world model for subsequent Model Predictive Control (MPC).

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for Personalized Robotic Manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in robotic tasks.
Investigates how embodied agents can follow user preferences in zero-shot learning scenarios, crucial for household robotics.

stories.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
stories.author: Bernie Wang
bullet_points: Introduces PathFM, a new trajectory-based forecasting model designed to address limitations in current time series foundation models.
PathFM utilizes flow matching to model the dependence structure of future multivariate trajectories, which is often unspecified in existing models.
This capability is crucial for predicting trajectory-dependent quantities like cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses routing exploration challenges in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It examines the tension between fine-grained expert segmentation (increasing expressiveness) and shared experts (universal activation).
The core problem identified is that shared experts can reduce the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of view-dependent features in 3D world models derived from Geometry Foundation Models (GFMs).
Introduces GeoState, a novel view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling.
Aims to separate scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation, improving prediction accuracy.

stories.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
stories.author: Yan Li
bullet_points: Introduces a robust Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework designed for adaptive treatment policies.
Addresses critical challenges in clinical AI, specifically model and measurement uncertainty in biomarker data.
Applies the framework to adaptive therapy for metastatic prostate cancer using a clinical simulator.

stories.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
stories.author: Omri Azencot
bullet_points: The paper addresses a key limitation in Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) regarding how temporal data is represented.
It proposes using 'complementary representations' as a design principle to improve time-series reasoning.
This approach aims to allow the model to selectively preserve necessary information while factoring out irrelevant variation for better task performance.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of distinguishing between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are those that support generalization beyond their initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The research proposes a method to study this distinction by artificially constructing new relations from existing ones.

stories.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces OmniVerifier-C1, a new decomposed graded verifier for generative world models.
Moves beyond binary (True/False) judgments to provide continuous, fine-grained critiques for multimodal AI.
Aims to enhance the robustness of visual verifiers when handling complex, compositional environmental rules.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
Addresses the gap in current benchmarks which rely on well-specified tasks, unlike real-world scenarios requiring ambiguity resolution.
Comprises 95 end-to-end delivery tasks derived from 20 customer scenarios across 18 different industries.

stories.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
stories.author: Pratham Yogish Maliya
bullet_points: The research investigates 'evaluation awareness' in LLMs—the tendency for models to detect when they are being tested.
Current research on this phenomenon is heavily biased towards English, neglecting the vast user base in Indic languages.
The study tests four instruction-tuned models across different families to see if evaluation awareness manifests differently in Indic languages.

stories.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
stories.author: Chien-Sheng Wu
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM applications for scientific ideation: optimizing for quality over diversity.
The study focuses on 'document-grounded ideation,' aiming to generate a set of ideas that are both high-quality and significantly distinct.
This work contributes to improving the initial, crucial ideation phase within automated scientific research pipelines.

stories.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: Introduces Market-Based Post-Training (MPT) to address limitations in current multi-agent systems.
MPT allows for the joint learning of individual agent action policies and the collective self-orchestration of decentralized agent swarms.
The framework uses a market-based mechanism where agents express participation willingness through bids.

stories.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
stories.author: Ricardo Rei
bullet_points: Introduces MindEval2, a new framework designed to rigorously evaluate Language Models (LLMs) used in mental health support.
Addresses limitations of current benchmarks, which rely on synthetic patients that may be unrealistically forthcoming.
Proposes clinically grounded rubrics to improve the transparency and practical utility of LLM evaluation in sensitive healthcare contexts.

stories.title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?
stories.author: Yue Zhao
bullet_points: Introduces Grid-Bench, a new executable benchmark designed to test LLMs on spatial reasoning.
The benchmark evaluates how accurately LLMs can predict the final state of discrete worlds after sequential spatial operations.
It tests transformations across 2D, 3D, and 4D grids using eight families of operations.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research distinguishes between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are those that support generalization beyond their initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study investigates this distinction by artificially constructing new relations from existing knowledge.
